translationRepairs: Kuai Tong said: "Lord Wu Xin of Zhao does not know my faults; he has sent to ask whether I still live. I am going to see him and urge this: 'If you insist on winning every battle before you take ground, on storming every wall before you accept surrender, I believe you court disaster.

Kuai Tong said: "Lord Wuxin of Zhao does not know my faults; he has sent to ask whether I still live. I am going to see him and urge this: 'If you insist on winning every battle before you take ground, on storming every wall before you accept surrender, I believe you court disaster.
武信君 is the title Lord Wuxin, rendered so in s0003.

You crossed the west-bank Yellow River, took the king of Wei, captured Xia Shuo, forced Jingxing, avenged Chen Yu's wrongs and bent Zhao to your will, overawed Yan and pacified Qi, shattered Chu hosts in the hundreds of thousands, struck down Long Ju, and wheeled west to answer the King of Han—achievements without parallel and stratagem seldom seen in any age.

You crossed the west-bank Yellow River, took the king of Wei, captured Xia Shuo, forced Jingxing, punished Chen Yu for his crimes and bent Zhao to your will, overawed Yan and pacified Qi, shattered Chu hosts in the hundreds of thousands, struck down Long Ju, and wheeled west to answer the King of Han—achievements without parallel and stratagem seldom seen in any age.
誅成安君之罪 means executing Chen Yu for his offenses, not avenging wrongs done to him.
Kuai Tong had long been friendly with the Qi scholar Ansheng, who once pressed his counsel on Xiang Yu—counsel Yu never adopted.
Kuai Tong had long been friendly with the Qi scholar An Qisheng, who once pressed his counsel on Xiang Yu—counsel Yu never adopted.

The king of Wu bore the Liu surname's honor of chief mourner, leaned on the gift of staff and stool to skip court, ruled four commanderies across thousands of li, coined money from his copper hills and salt from his boiling pans, built a fleet from Jiangling timber, grew rich and strong, bought allies among the kingdoms, joined the seven-state league, marched west, took Daliang, broke the army at Hufu, then fled headlong until Yue ran him down at Dantu—head severed from body, line extinguished, a cautionary tale for the world.

The king of Wu bore the title Libationer of the Liu clan, leaned on the gift of staff and stool to skip court, ruled four commanderies across thousands of li, coined money from his copper hills and salt from his boiling pans, built a fleet from Jiangling timber, grew rich and strong, bought allies among the kingdoms, joined the seven-state league, marched west, took Daliang, broke the army at Hufu, then fled headlong until Yue ran him down at Dantu—head severed from body, line extinguished, a cautionary tale for the world.
祭酒 is Libationer, a senior honorific of the clan, not a mourner.
息夫躬 is Xifu Gong, as s0280 renders it.
Zi Hui schemed for Qi and left Duke Yin of Lu exposed; Luan Shu framed the Xi clan and Duke Li of Jin died for it.
Zi Hui schemed with Huan and left Duke Yin of Lu exposed; Luan Shu framed the Xi clan and Duke Li of Jin died for it.
謀桓 means plotting with (Duke) Huan of Lu; Qi is not mentioned.
Shu Niu harried Zhong until Uncle Sun died;
Shu Niu harried Zhong until Shusun died;
叔孫 is Shusun (Bao), a clan name, not 'Uncle Sun'.
Yi Li faked a blood oath and Heir Zhu of Song died for it;
Yi Li faked a blood oath and Heir Cuo of Song died for it;
宋痤 is Cuo, heir of Song.
